questions.q: What is the main problem with order-service's original print() logging, as this lab frames it?
options: It writes to stdout instead of stderr
It runs too slowly under load
It only works on Windows containers
It carries no timestamp discipline, no request correlation, and nothing machine-queryable
questions.explain: Plain print() lines have no structure a query engine can filter on and no shared ID tying lines from the same request together -- exactly what the JSON formatter and request_id fix.

questions.q: Why does the lab add a custom order_checkout_duration_seconds histogram instead of relying only on AKS's built-in CPU and memory metrics?
options: Because AKS metrics are always wrong
Because platform metrics can't see inside the request to measure how long the application's own checkout logic actually took
Because histograms are required for every Kubernetes pod
Because CPU and memory metrics are deprecated
questions.explain: Platform defaults show resource usage, not application-level behavior -- a custom histogram is the only way to measure checkout duration from the application's own point of view.

questions.q: Why does charge_card get its own trace span instead of being left as untimed code inside the checkout handler?
options: Spans are mandatory for every function call in Python
It's the riskiest, most likely-to-be-slow downstream call, so isolating it shows whether it dominates the parent request's total time
Trace spans replace the need for logging entirely
Azure Monitor refuses to accept traces without a child span
questions.explain: Wrapping the risky call in its own span is what lets a slow payment call show up as the one child span dominating the parent's duration, the same pattern Lesson 1's inventory-service example demonstrated.

questions.q: What does configure_azure_monitor(), called once at process startup, actually do?
options: It deletes old telemetry from Application Insights
It only configures logging, not metrics or traces
It points the OpenTelemetry SDK's exporters at the Application Insights resource using one connection string, for all three signal types
It replaces the need for a connection string entirely
questions.explain: One configuration call wires structured logs, the custom histogram, and trace spans all through the same Application Insights connection string.

questions.q: In the verification KQL query, what does filtering on one OperationId actually prove?
options: That the three pillars were pulled back out correlated together, from the same real checkout, using one shared ID
That Application Insights has unlimited storage
That logs and metrics cannot share an ID with traces
That the query only works if traces are disabled
questions.explain: The real proof of the lab isn't that each pillar exists in isolation -- it's that one OperationId retrieves the log line, the metric recording, and the span for the same request, in order.
